content: {"argument": "The witness tests a hostname with a single-character subdomain ('a'), but the updated regex requires labels to be at least two characters long ([a-z\\-\\d]{2,63}), which no longer matches 'www.a.com'. However, the original regex also imposed a minimum length via [a-z\\-\\d]{1,63}, so the change inadvertently tightened the constraint. Since the PR title indicates a refactoring of URL normalization edge handling, and the test uses an edge case (single-character label) that may not be a common or intended use case, the behavior change could be considered acceptable if the regex now better aligns with hostname label standards (though note: single-character labels are technically allowed). Nevertheless, because the change breaks a previously passing test for a valid input and no announcement indicates this tightening was intentional, the defense cannot fully justify the regression.", "concedes": true}
